name: Zen Technologies Limited

what_it_is.prose: Zen Technologies Limited is a Hyderabad-headquartered, BSE/NSE-listed defence OEM founded in 1993. The company operates two principal product lines: counter-UAS (the Zen Anti-Drone System / ZADS — Atlas slug cus-003) and defence training simulators (the largest portfolio of its kind in India, including the Armoured Combat Training Simulator, Live Ranges, and Live & Virtual Simulation systems). Zen also produces a family of Remote Controlled Weapon Stations (RCWS) — Parashu (7.62x51 MMG), Fanish (12.7x108 HMG tank-mounted), Sharur (12.7x99 naval), Prahasta, Hawkeye, and Durgam rugged camera. The company is AS9100D, ISO/IEC 27001, and CMMI Maturity Level 5 certified, with a US subsidiary (Zen Technologies USA Inc). For FY26, Zen reported revenue of ₹687.7 crore (down 29.4% year-on-year) and a closing order book of ₹1,336 crore (approximately 2x FY26 revenue, giving 3-4 years revenue visibility). Q1 FY27 order book was ₹1,239.02 crore as of 30 June 2026. The ZADS platform entered Indian Air Force service in 2021 and has since received multiple follow-on contracts including a ₹289 crore counter-drone contract in November 2025 and a ₹404 crore defence orders package in January 2026 (of which ₹332 crore was for anti-drone systems and ₹72 crore for simulators).

deployments_procurement.summary: Zen Technologies' counter-drone business is anchored by recurring Ministry of Defence orders. The first ZADS order was placed by the Indian Air Force in 2021 as part of more than ₹300 crore in armed forces orders. A follow-on procurement order from the Ministry of Defence was placed in September 2023. The Indian Army's Army Air Defence College at Gopalpur received hard-kill variants from mid-2024. A ₹289 crore counter-drone contract was signed in November 2025, followed by a ₹404 crore defence orders package in January 2026 (₹332 crore anti-drone + ₹72 crore simulators). The Q1 FY27 NSE IPCL filing dated 26 July 2026 reported an order book of ₹1,239.02 crore.

import_dependencies.summary: Zen Technologies is AS9100D, ISO/IEC 27001, and CMMI Maturity Level 5 certified, with approximately 90%+ indigenous content on its simulator product line. For the ZADS counter-UAS platform specifically, the principal imported subsystems are EO/IR gimbals and thermal imaging cores (typically sourced from Teledyne FLIR, Controp, or SCD — USA / Israel / Belgium), RF detector SDR front-ends (Ettus / National Instruments / RTL-SDR — USA / Taiwan), and FPGA for signal processing (Xilinx / AMD — USA). The 12.7 mm heavy machine gun used in the kinetic hard-kill variant is a domestically-produced or licensed-pattern weapon.

faq.question: Why did Zen Technologies' FY26 revenue decline?
faq.answer: Zen Technologies reported FY26 revenue of ₹687.7 crore, down 29.4% year-on-year, with PAT also down 31% YoY. The Q4 FY26 results were particularly weak, with PAT plunging 69% YoY, causing shares to tumble 11% on 4 May 2026. The decline was attributed to revenue timing — large counter-drone orders booked in late FY26 (₹289 cr November 2025, ₹404 cr January 2026) had not yet converted to recognised revenue. The Q1 FY27 order book of ₹1,239 crore (≈2x FY26 revenue) signals recovery visibility.

faq.question: What is Zen Technologies' product portfolio beyond ZADS?
faq.answer: Beyond the Zen Anti-Drone System (ZADS), Zen Technologies operates two other major product lines: defence training simulators (the largest portfolio of its kind in India, including the Armoured Combat Training Simulator, Live Ranges, and Live & Virtual Simulation systems) and a family of Remote Controlled Weapon Stations (RCWS) — Parashu (7.62x51 MMG), Fanish (12.7x108 HMG tank-mounted), Sharur (12.7x99 naval), Prahasta, Hawkeye, and Durgam rugged camera. The company is AS9100D, ISO/IEC 27001, and CMMI Maturity Level 5 certified.

faq.question: What is Zen Technologies' relationship with the Indian armed forces?
faq.answer: Zen Technologies has been a long-standing supplier to the Indian armed forces since 1993. The company is the official trainer for Indian Army mechanised forces (Armoured Combat Training Simulator, Live Ranges, Live & Virtual Simulation) and the Indian Air Force (first ZADS order 2021). Zen also supplies the NSG with the Vajra Shot handheld anti-drone gun (a BBBS product, not Zen — correction: Zen's RCWS family includes Parashu, Fanish, Sharur, Prahasta, Hawkeye, and Durgam). The company is AS9100D, ISO/IEC 27001, and CMMI Maturity Level 5 certified, with a US subsidiary (Zen Technologies USA Inc).
